The incident involved a 31-year-old suspect who tried to breach security at the Washington Hilton, where scores of journalists, politicians, and celebrities were gathered. **Vice President JD Vance** was evacuated before Trump, sparking controversy over security arrangements.  The attack has fueled political debate about the role of media in reporting on the incident and the president's response to it.

recent_articles.title: Pro-choice campaigners in Malta create lockboxes containing abortion pills | Malta | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Women on Waves**, a Netherlands-based charity, has affixed lockboxes containing abortion pills to sites across **Malta** in a campaign designed to highlight the country's near-total ban on abortion. The campaign, which aims to provide practical help to women seeking abortions under the strict laws of the country, has resulted in 16 women contacting the organization in its first eight days.  The campaign has sparked debate and prompted an anti-abortion group to call for police intervention. **Doctors for Choice Malta**, a local organization advocating for abortion rights, reports that many women are forced to choose between complying with the law or their right to decide.

recent_articles.title: Michael Jackson biopic smashes box office record
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The new **Michael Jackson** biopic, "Michael," has smashed box office records with a $217 million opening weekend globally. The film, starring **Jaafar Jackson**, surpassed previous record holders like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "Oppenheimer." Despite mixed reviews from critics, the film's audience reception was overwhelmingly positive, earning it a 97% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.  The film focuses heavily on Jackson's musical career, including recreated concert performances and explores his strained relationship with his father.

recent_articles.title: Sun Pharma shares jump over 9% after firm announces $12 billion Organon acquisition - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sun Pharma** announced the completion of a definitive agreement to acquire **Organon**, a US-based company specializing in women's health, for $12 billion. The transaction will be completed through a merger of Organon with a subsidiary of **Sun Pharma**.  The combined entity will become one of the top 25 global pharmaceutical companies and a leader in women's health with a strong portfolio of biosimilars.  **Sun Pharma** executive chairman, Dilip Shanghvi, expressed confidence that the acquisition will strengthen the company's global business and drive long-term growth. The deal is expected to close in early 2027.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court takes suo motu note of assault on woman advocate, issues directions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** took suo motu action in a brutal assault case involving a woman advocate in New Delhi, directing the Delhi Police Commissioner to hand over the investigation to a senior officer. The court also ordered the police to look into three hospitals' refusal of admission to the victim and investigate allegations against her husband's in-laws regarding the disappearance of her two minor children. **Manoj Kumar**, the alleged assailant, was arrested on April 26th after confessing to stabbing his wife on April 22nd during a family dispute.

recent_articles.title: Men accused of raping cellmates mistakenly allowed to stay in shared cells by Queensland prison staff | Prisons | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Queensland Corrective Services** has been criticized by an ombudsman's report for allowing prisoners to share cells despite strict protocols, citing overcrowding and concerns about documenting sexual assault allegations. The report found that **prisoners**, often double-celled due to capacity issues, were sometimes placed in shared cells after alleged assaults, with one prisoner later charged with rape after being transferred to another facility under investigation.  The ombudsman also highlighted health facility deficiencies and complaints of undercooked chicken served at the Brisbane correctional center.

recent_articles.title: Two women’s quest for justice for their daughters fuels Bengal poll fight - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Two mothers from West Bengal, **Ratna Debnath** and **Sabina Yasmin**, are contesting the Assembly elections to seek justice for their daughters' deaths. **Debnath**, whose daughter was murdered in a hospital attack, is campaigning on behalf of the **BJP**.  **Yasmin**, whose daughter died in a bomb attack during victory celebrations, is running as a candidate for the **Left Front**. Both mothers blame the ruling **Trinamool Congress** and Chief Minister **Mamata Banerjee** for their daughters' deaths. Their campaigns highlight concerns about political violence and accountability within the state.

recent_articles.title: From syringes to stents: Iran war exposes NHS dependency on petrochemicals | NHS | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The war in Iran has caused disruptions to global supply chains, leading to concerns about shortages and rising costs for medical products. The **NHS** is particularly vulnerable due to its reliance on petrochemicals and the fact that it's one of the world's largest bulk buyers of medical supplies.  While the NHS has increased purchases of drugs and devices to build up buffers, experts warn that sustained disruption could lead to shortages in gloves, catheters, and other essential items. The price of many common medical items has jumped since the war broke out, with shortages anticipated for surgical masks, gowns, and bandages. The **NHS** is working closely with suppliers to minimize the impact of cost pressures and ensure trusts are not required to change clinical practice unnecessarily.

recent_articles.title: ‘Sludge in the system’: myriad problems stymie Labour’s 1.5m new homes pledge | Construction industry | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The UK's housing crisis is being exacerbated by a combination of factors, including a skills shortage, rising material costs, and affordability concerns. Despite government pledges to build 1.5 million new homes, the pace of construction remains sluggish.  A lack of affordable housing options and high costs are hindering progress. While planning reforms have been implemented to streamline development processes, they haven't yet addressed underlying issues such as supply chain disruptions and rising material prices. The industry is facing a significant cost of doing business crisis, with many developers struggling to make projects viable. Experts warn that the government needs to address these challenges to achieve its housing targets.

recent_articles.title: Ashok Kharat case: Oshnology and other deceptions of a godman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ashokkumar Kharat**, a godman, was granted judicial custody after being brought to the Nashik District Sessions Court for charges of sexual assault and forced abortion. The **prosecution**, led by **Shailendra Bagade** and **Kiran Bendbhar**, accused him of these crimes.  The case is ongoing with Kharat appearing via videoconference the following day.

recent_articles.title: Youth sentenced to 20 years rigorous imprisonment in POCSO case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old man, **Sabanna Kattimani**, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for kidnapping and sexually assaulting a minor girl.  **Justice Muhammad Mujeer Ullah C.G.** found him guilty under the POCSO Act and imposed a fine of ₹1.25 lakh. The investigation was led by Circle Police Inspector **Raghavendra H.S.** of the Ratkal police station, and the case was prosecuted by **Shantveer B. Thuppad**, representing the State.  The court also ordered compensation for the victim from the Legal Services Authority.
